points.heading: Deepen: two-word times
points.body:
Today we deepen our work with compound tenses. A compound tense has two parts: a helper form of haber and a participle. The participle is the completed form of a verb, such as cantado, comido, or vivido. In «he cantado», he is the helper and cantado is the participle.

The helper moves the action through time. «He cantado» connects a completed action with now. «Había cantado» places it before another past moment. «Habré cantado» looks ahead, and «habría cantado» describes what would happen in a condition. The participle stays unchanged in all four forms.

Practice: Write «he comido», «habías comido», «habremos comido», and «habría comido». Circle the helper, underline the participle, and write one true sentence with «he comido».

Common mistake: Adding a plural ending to the participle. Write «hemos comido», not «hemos comidos».

lesson.summary: Compound tenses combine haber with a participle. The helper shows the time, while the participle keeps the completed action.
